title: Lowest common ancestor

hook.scenario: Two branches in Git split from a common commit 50 commits ago. To merge them, Git needs to find the exact point where their paths diverged.
hook.question: How do you find the lowest node in a tree that has two target nodes as descendants?

why_it_exists.problem: Finding the shared origin of two nodes by traversing parent pointers requires extra memory or parent pointers that standard binary trees do not store.
why_it_exists.naive_solution: Storing root-to-node paths for both nodes in lists, then scanning the lists to find the last common node (uses extra O(n) space).
why_it_exists.better_idea: Use top-down BST splitting logic for BSTs (O(1) extra space), or post-order bottom-up recursion for general binary trees to identify the exact node where p and q diverge.

mental_model.intuition: Find the split point: the lowest node where target p and target q branch off in different directions.
mental_model.description: For BSTs: start at root; if both p and q are smaller than node.val, move left; if both are larger, move right; as soon as p and q split (or one equals node.val), node is the LCA. For general trees: post-order recurse; if a node finds p or q in its left subtree AND right subtree, that node is the LCA.
mental_model.repeated_decision: are p and q both on the same side of this node, or does this node split them?

explanation:
The Lowest Common Ancestor (LCA) of two nodes `p` and `q` is defined as the deepest node in the tree that has both `p` and `q` as descendants (where a node is allowed to be a descendant of itself).

Case 1: LCA in a Binary Search Tree (O(h) time, O(1) space)
Because a BST is ordered:
1. If `p.val < node.val` and `q.val < node.val`, both targets lie in the left subtree -> move `node = node.left`.
2. If `p.val > node.val` and `q.val > node.val`, both targets lie in the right subtree -> move `node = node.right`.
3. Otherwise, `p` and `q` split (or one equals `node.val`). `node` IS the LCA!

Case 2: LCA in a General Binary Tree (O(n) time, O(h) space)
When no search ordering exists, use bottom-up post-order recursion:
`def lca(node, p, q)`:
- `if not node or node == p or node == q: return node`
- `left = lca(node.left, p, q)`
- `right = lca(node.right, p, q)`
- `if left and right: return node` (Both subtrees found a target -> `node` is LCA!)
- `return left if left else right` (Pass found target upwards)

Walkthrough on General Tree:
Tree:
       3
      / \
     5   1
    / \
   6   2
  LCA of 6 and 2:
- Call on root `3`: recurse left to `5` and right to `1`.
- At `5`: recurse left to `6` (matches `p`, returns `6`) and right to `2` (matches `q`, returns `2`).
- At `5`: `left` is `6` and `right` is `2`. Both non-null -> `5` returns itself as LCA!
- At `3`: `left` returns `5`, `right` returns `None`. Return `5` as final answer.

key_points.title: Self-Ancestry
key_points.detail: A node can be its own descendant. If p is an ancestor of q, LCA(p, q) = p.

key_points.title: BST Split Point
key_points.detail: In a BST, LCA is the first node where p and q are no longer on the same side.

key_points.title: General Tree Post-Order Convergence
key_points.detail: In a general tree, LCA is the first node where left and right recursive calls both return non-null nodes.

common_mistakes.title: Assuming LCA cannot be p or q itself
common_mistakes.explanation: If node p is an ancestor of node q, then LCA(p, q) is p itself. Assuming LCA must be a parent above both p and q causes incorrect null returns.

common_mistakes.title: Applying BST split logic to a non-BST binary tree
common_mistakes.explanation: Comparing node values to p and q relies on BST sortedness. Applying this to a general tree yields invalid search directions.

common_mistakes.title: Assuming parent pointers exist
common_mistakes.explanation: Standard binary tree nodes only store `left` and `right` child pointers, requiring top-down or bottom-up traversal.

when_not_to_use.scenario: Graphs with cycles or multiple paths without tree properties
when_not_to_use.reason: General LCA algorithms assume a single unique root path tree DAG structure.

failure_signals: Problem asks for the common origin or lowest ancestor of two elements in a tree structure.

engineering_examples.title: Git Merge-Base Calculation (`git merge-base`)
engineering_examples.problem: Find the common ancestor commit of two branches to compute a 3-way git merge diff.
engineering_examples.why_this_algorithm: Commits in Git form a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) tree structure where `git merge-base` calculates the LCA of two commit hashes.

engineering_examples.title: UI Event Bubbling / Common Container
engineering_examples.problem: Find the lowest DOM element container encompassing two clicked UI components.
engineering_examples.why_this_algorithm: DOM tree LCA finds the nearest enclosing parent element to apply event handling or focus scope.

BST split point or post-order match

recall_questions.q: What is the definition of Lowest Common Ancestor (LCA) of nodes p and q?
recall_questions.answer: The deepest node in the tree that has both p and q as descendants.

recall_questions.q: How do you find the LCA of two nodes in a Binary Search Tree (BST)?
recall_questions.answer: Walk down from the root: if both p and q are smaller than current node go left, if both are larger go right, otherwise the current node is the LCA split point.

recall_questions.q: In general binary tree LCA recursion, how do you know when a node is the LCA?
recall_questions.answer: When recursive calls on its left and right subtrees both return non-null nodes.

oa_questions.question: Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Search Tree: Given a BST and nodes p and q, find their LCA.
oa_questions.answer: Start at root. Iteratively move to left child if both p,q < root.val, or right child if both p,q > root.val. Return current node when they split.
oa_questions.approach: Iterative BST search split point in O(h) time, O(1) space.

oa_questions.question: Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Tree: Given a general binary tree and nodes p and q, find their LCA.
oa_questions.answer: Use bottom-up DFS recursion. If node is None, p, or q, return node. Recurse left and right. If both return non-null, current node is LCA.
oa_questions.approach: Post-order bottom-up DFS tracking subtree target matches.

interesting_facts: In competitive programming, LCA queries on static trees can be answered in O(1) time after O(n log n) precomputation using binary lifting or Euler tour + RMQ!
